newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bamerindus awaits Cenbank loan rules - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bamerindus awaits Cenbank loan rules - paper.

text.p: Ailing Brazilian bank Bamerindus is awaiting the Central Bank to set the conditions for a $2.0-3.0 billion 90-day credit line to help it overcome its liquidity troubles, O Globo daily said.

Citing market sources, the newspaper said the Central Bank is not expected to require a change of ownership but it will call for Bamerindus majority shareholder Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira to give up making decisions regarding the bank's management.
The loan would be under the Central Bank's medium-term financial assistance, which is earmarked for banks under restructuring plans, O Globo said.

The credit line would be tied to a new interest rate called TBAN and would be valid for 90 days but renewable for 90 more days, which would allow Bamerindus to buy time for further restructuring and restoring public confidence, it added.
According to the newspaper, the loan would be used by Bamerindus to pay off its debts with state-run bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) in the interbank market.
O Globo also said Bamerindus has already sent to the Central Bank a proposal for adjustment which includes cutting costs, closing branches and increasing revenues.

Bamerindus Group has recently reorganized assets in a move to strengthen Bamerindus bank, Brazil's fourth-largest private institution. But the bank was expected to do more, as it still needs an injection of money to solve its recognized liquidity problems.

No Central Bank officials were immediately available for comment on the report. At Bamerindus, press officials confirmed talks with the Central Bank but they could not disclose the content of the negotiations.
